In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
zwitterionic surface chemistry is the most effective antifouling coating, followed by amphiphilic and hydrophilic coatings in decreasing order of effectiveness.
the antifouling mechanism of zwitterionic coatings is a result of electrostatic repulsion, and that the amphiphilic coatings resist biofouling by the formation of a hydrophobic surface.
zwitterionic and hydrophilic coatings are effective at reducing the fouling of single protein molecules, but the amphiphilic coatings are more resistant to the fouling of bacteria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amphiphilic iCVD coatings have a lower surface energy and a higher surface roughness, which are responsible for their lower fouling propensity.
the amphiphilic films are more effective than the zwitterionic films at preventing protein adhesion and that the amphiphile films are more hydrophilic than the zwitterion films.
the amphiphilic iCVD thin films are more resistant to fouling than the zwitterionic iCVD thin film, and the amphiphilicity of the surface is a critical component for the fouling resistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the antifouling properties of zwitterionic coatings are governed by their ability to resist protein adsorption and the amphiphilic coatings are governed by the ability to resist the formation of protein adlayers.
zwitterionic and hydrophilic surfaces are not always antifouling.
amphiphilic thin films have a higher antifouling resistance than hydrophilic zwitterionic thin films.
